thread:
jordan: noticed weirdness in the console: after a ws reconnect some latency buckets go stale and autoscaler spikes. screenshots in #observability but here's the short repro
priya: hmm, that's worrying. is it the client doing a reconnect or our LB routing?
elena: my hunch: when route flips we emit a new connection but the histogram aggregation key doesn't include session_id, so the old buckets stick around and get attributed to the new route. autoscaler reads the bucket totals -> overreacts.
jordan: exact sequence: user opens ws, route=A, we record latency bucket tag route=A. route flip -> client reconnects to route=B, but the dashboard still shows many A-bucket tokens for that tenant for ~2m. autoscaler uses tenant:sum(latency_bucket) and scales out.
sam: that's bad. do we have logs that show the tag mismatch? any example?
elena: yes, from staging: ``[2026-04-01T12:03:15Z] conn_id=abc123 route=A latency_ms=120 bucket=100-200 tenant=acme`` then after reconnect ``[2026-04-01T12:03:40Z] conn_id=def456 route=B latency_ms=30 bucket=0-50 tenant=acme`` but metric exporter keeps a cached labelset for the tenant->route=A for another minute.
priya: is this prometheus/client_golang label cardinality or our aggregator TTL? we recently changed the histogram shard TTL to 90s.
elena: aggregator TTL is 90s, but we also have a separate rollout that started deduping metrics by `connection_fingerprint` which was introduced last week. fingerprint collides across routes for short windows.
jordan: how often do autoscaler queries run? can we short-circuit until fixed?
sam: scaling queries every 30s. mitigation: add a query filter to ignore buckets older than 45s, but console UI needs accurate timeline too. not ideal.
priya: quick mitigation plan: (1) patch aggregator to include `session_id` (or route+conn_id) in the key so buckets are isolated; (2) add a temporary dashboard panel that uses `max_over_time(latency_bucket[1m])` instead of raw sum; (3) add alert if route delta > 30% post-reconnect.
elena: agreement. I can PR the aggregator change, it's low-risk but needs a canary.
jordan: tagging @sam for rollout approval — we need a controlled canary to avoid metric explosion.
sam: ok approve canary. deploy plan: canary 5% -> watch metric churn and autoscale events for 15m -> 50% -> 100%. ops-bot: scheduled canary start at 2026-04-01T14:00:00Z (ID: canary-5247).
priya: I'll add the dashboard panel and a PromQL snippet for the mitigation: ``sum by(tenant,route) (rate(latency_bucket_sum[1m])) / sum by(tenant,route) (rate(latency_bucket_count[1m]))`` and the temporary filter: ``and timestamp() - max_over_time(ts{job=\"aggregator\"}[1m]) < 45`` (pseudo).
elena: reproduction steps in staging: 
```
# open sse/ws and wait for route flip
curl -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \"https://staging.redwood/api/v1/stream?tenant=acme\" -v
# then flip route via test-proxy
test-proxy route set acme B
# observe metrics via grafana panel
```

jordan: can we add a unit test for aggregator TTL + label churn? last time a similar change regressed.
elena: yes, I'll add a regression test that simulates fingerprint collision + route flip, asserting no leak of old labelset after TTL.
sam: who owns verification during canary? jordan, you good to watch autoscale alerts?
jordan: yep I'll monitor and have rollback playbook ready.
priya: I'll also add a short-term rate-limiter on autoscaler decisions: require 2 consecutive high reads before scaling up to avoid reacting to transient label churn.
ops-bot: reminder: oncall rotation starts 2026-04-02. If canary overlaps, escalate to @oncall.
jordan: timeline: elena PR today, priya dashboard change + query patch today, canary at 14:00. afterwards track for 4 hours then roll forward.
elena: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/aggregator/pull/412 (WIP) — adding session_id key and regression tests.
priya: created dashboard panel draft: https://grafana.redwood/d/streams/latency-reconnect?panelId=7
sam: thanks team. once canary passes let's also add a console note explaining why some historic buckets may look noisy during rollouts. UX will get questions.
jordan: good call. I'll draft the note after canary.
priya: any objections to backport to 1.8? some customers on 1.8 private deployments.
elena: backportable, but need a small patch + test, will open backport PR after main merges.
sam: approved. no objections.
jordan: cool. I'll update status channel when canary starts.
ops-bot: canary event: canary-5247 STARTED by sam at 2026-04-01T14:00:05Z
priya: seeing lower churn already in staging after local agg tweak. hopeful.
elena: merging PR to canary ring now.
jordan: monitoring dashboards... all good so far, no autoscale blips first 10m.
sam: keep watching for 30m. if anything suspicious ping #incidents.
priya: noted. will follow up with post-mortem if needed.
